3	/// How the Media tab's list is narrowed and ordered (road map 2's phase 8c):
4	/// a search over names, a sort, and the "unused only" switch.
5	///
6	/// A VALUE, in `AudioNormalize.swift`'s and `CaptionLayout.swift`'s shape —
7	/// media in, ids out — for the reason those two are values: the arithmetic is
8	/// then a function anybody can read, run and check without a panel, and the
9	/// pane above it does nothing but hand rows to the answer. It is also the
10	/// only way the ordering rules below can ever be measured, since a list of
11	/// rows in a scroll view is not something a proof script can interrogate.
12	///
13	/// **It is view state and it is not persisted**, which is a decision rather
14	/// than an omission. Three arguments, in the order they were made:
15	/// a search is an act of FINDING and not a preference, and a panel that comes
16	/// back tomorrow showing two of a project's forty files — because of what
17	/// somebody typed once — is a bug report about missing media; the pane is
18	/// rebuilt per document window, so two open projects filter independently,
19	/// which is what "the Media tab of THIS project" means; and a `UserDefaults`
20	/// key would have to be pinned in the offscreen harness's `pinDefaults` or
21	/// every chrome render of this pane would depend on whatever the machine
22	/// happened to store (app/CLAUDE.md's rule for the keys the chrome reads).
23	/// Nothing here writes a default and nothing reads one.
24	struct MediaListFilter: Equatable {
25	    /// The sort popup's rows, in menu order; the raw value IS the row index,
26	    /// so the order is API for the popup that reads it.
27	    ///
28	    /// **`importOrder` is spelled "Import Order" and not "Added"**, which the
29	    /// road map's own wording ("name, duration, added, kind") would have
30	    /// suggested, because the app knows an ORDER and does not know a TIME.
31	    /// Nothing records when a media entry arrived: `MediaSnapshot` and the
32	    /// core's `Media` are the same eleven keys and none of them is a
33	    /// timestamp. What the media array carries instead is insertion order —
34	    /// `add_media` pushes after `allocate_id` (`core/src/edit_track.rs`),
35	    /// `absorb_media` does the same (`edit_paste.rs`), `remove_media` retains
36	    /// and `relink_media` mutates in place, so nothing ever reorders it — and
37	    /// for any project built by ops that is also ascending id order. A real
38	    /// "date added" would be a persisted field, which is a version-7 schema
39	    /// bump, and phase 8 is declared "no schema; view state throughout": a
40	    /// row that says what the app actually knows is worth more than a row
41	    /// that says what the road map wished it knew.
42	    enum Order: Int, CaseIterable {
43	        case importOrder, name, duration, kind
44	
45	        var title: String {
46	            switch self {
47	            case .importOrder: return "Import Order"
48	            case .name: return "Name"
49	            case .duration: return "Duration"
50	            case .kind: return "Kind"
51	            }
52	        }
53	    }
54	
55	    /// What was typed in the search field, verbatim. Not trimmed: the field
56	    /// is on screen beside the list, and a filter that quietly ignored a
57	    /// space somebody typed would disagree with what they can see. Empty is
58	    /// the only value that means "no search".
59	    var search = ""
60	    var order = Order.importOrder
61	    var unusedOnly = false
62	
63	    /// Whether the list is showing less than the project holds — what the
64	    /// item count says out loud, so "3 of 40 items" never appears over a
65	    /// list that is showing everything.
66	    var isNarrowing: Bool { !search.isEmpty || unusedOnly }
67	
68	    /// Whether one entry survives the two filters.
69	    ///
70	    /// The name test is `localizedStandardContains`, which is the comparison
71	    /// Finder searches with: case-insensitive, diacritic-insensitive and
72	    /// width-insensitive against the current locale, so `resume` finds
73	    /// `Résumé.mov` and `KEYNOTE` finds `keynote.mov`. Spelling it out as
74	    /// `range(of:options:)` would be the same three options with a fourth
75	    /// chance to forget one.
76	    ///
77	    /// "Unused" is `ProjectSnapshot.usesMedia`, which walks the nests as well
78	    /// as the timeline (`MediaUsage.swift`) — so a file that appears only
79	    /// inside a compound clip is USED and is not offered up for deletion by
80	    /// this filter, which is exactly what `remove_media` will say if it is
81	    /// asked.
82	    func admits(_ entry: MediaSnapshot, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
83	        if unusedOnly, snapshot.usesMedia(entry.id) { return false }
84	        guard !search.isEmpty else { return true }
85	        return entry.name.localizedStandardContains(search)
86	    }
87	
88	    /// The ids of `media` in the order the list should show them — every id,
89	    /// filtered or not, because hiding a row and moving it are two different
90	    /// jobs and the pane does them separately.
91	    ///
92	    /// **Every order is ascending and every tie falls back to import order**,
93	    /// which is one rule rather than four opinions: a list of a few dozen
94	    /// files reads as well from either end, and "longest first" versus
95	    /// "shortest first" is an argument with no answer that would then have to
96	    /// be re-had for kind. The tiebreak is not decoration —
97	    /// `Array.sort` is not documented stable, so without it two files of the
98	    /// same duration could swap places between two runs of the same sort,
99	    /// which is the kind of thing nobody reports and everybody notices.
100	    func ordered(_ media: [MediaSnapshot]) -> [UInt32] {
101	        guard order != .importOrder else { return media.map { $0.id } }
102	        return media.enumerated().sorted { a, b in
103	            switch order {
104	            case .importOrder:
105	                return a.offset < b.offset
106	            case .name:
107	                let compared = a.element.name.localizedStandardCompare(b.element.name)
108	                if compared == .orderedSame { return a.offset < b.offset }
109	                return compared == .orderedAscending
110	            case .duration:
111	                return a.element.duration == b.element.duration
112	                    ? a.offset < b.offset : a.element.duration < b.element.duration
113	            case .kind:
114	                let left = a.element.kind.displayName
115	                let right = b.element.kind.displayName
116	                return left == right ? a.offset < b.offset : left < right
117	            }
118	        }.map { $0.element.id }
119	    }
120	}

124	extension MediaListFilter {
125	    /// The three controls of the Media tab's find band, built over a filter
126	    /// somebody else owns: `current` hands the value over, `apply` takes the
127	    /// new one back and is expected to re-arrange the list.
128	    ///
129	    /// They live beside the value rather than in `MediaPane.swift` for the
130	    /// reason `OptionControls.swift` exists at all — a control here stores
131	    /// nothing, so a control and the value it edits are one idea — and
132	    /// because the pane was at its size cap before this phase and this is the
133	    /// half of the band that is about the FILTER rather than about the panel's
134	    /// chrome. What the pane keeps is the layout: which line each control
135	    /// sits on, and the caption and the spacer around them.
136	    ///
137	    /// Each control writes THROUGH `apply` rather than mutating and then
138	    /// telling somebody — one path in, so a re-arrangement can never be
139	    /// skipped by a control that forgot to call back.
140	    static func controls(
141	        current: @escaping () -> MediaListFilter, apply: @escaping (MediaListFilter) -> Void
142	    ) -> (search: NSView, sort: NSView, unusedOnly: NSView) {
143	        let search = MediaSearchField(
144	            text: current().search,
145	            changed: { text in
146	                var next = current()
147	                next.search = text
148	                apply(next)
149	            })
150	        search.toolTip = "Show only files whose name contains this text"
151	
152	        let sort = OptionPopupControl(
153	            width: InspectorMetrics.popupWidth,
154	            items: Order.allCases.map { $0.title },
155	            read: { current().order.rawValue },
156	            write: { index in
157	                guard let order = Order(rawValue: index) else { return }
158	                var next = current()
159	                next.order = order
160	                apply(next)
161	            },
162	            enabled: { true }, onEdit: {})
163	        // The offscreen harness finds this popup by the tooltip's opening words
164	        // (`tools/proof/harness/main.swift`'s `mediaFilter`): reword both.

189	/// `controlTextDidEndEditing`, and `OptionFieldControl` is the same shape

196	/// (`MediaListFilter.search`); this field is handed the current one at build

198	/// value" rule the rest of the inspector is built on (`InspectorPane.swift`).

200	/// the media list changes, which destroys this view, and a search that lived
201	/// in the field would be lost with it while the list stayed narrowed.
202	///
203	/// Escape clears rather than reverting. AppKit's default for a text field is
204	/// to put back the value the field started editing with and end editing,
205	/// which for a search box means "undo my typing" where every other app on
206	/// this machine means "show me everything again".

209	/// class draws its own bezel, magnifier and cancel button and would be the
210	/// only system-looking control in a panel whose every field is

212	/// and it sends its action on a TIMER by default, which is a second answer to
213	/// "when does the list narrow" living somewhere this file cannot see. What it
214	/// would have brought for free is the cancel button and the recent-searches
215	/// menu; the first is Escape here and the second is not wanted in a list of a
216	/// few dozen files.

218	    private let changed: (String) -> Void

220	    init(text: String, changed: @escaping (String) -> Void) {
221	        self.changed = changed
222	        super.init(frame: .zero)
223	        DSField.style(self, height: 24, radius: DS.controlRadius, font: DS.sans(11))
224	        placeholderString = "Search by name"
225	        stringValue = text
226	        delegate = self
227	    }

229	    @available(*, unavailable)
230	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
231	        fatalError("MediaSearchField does not support NSCoder")
232	    }
233	
234	    func controlTextDidChange(_ obj: Notification) {
235	        changed(stringValue)
236	    }
237	
238	    func control(
239	        _ control: NSControl, textView: NSTextView, doCommandBy commandSelector: Selector
240	    ) -> Bool {
241	        guard commandSelector == #selector(NSResponder.cancelOperation(_:)) else { return false }
242	        // Handled here rather than by letting the field editor end: an empty
243	        // field with the caret still in it is what a person pressing Escape in

253	/// "Is this media used, and by what?" — the ONE spelling of a question the
254	/// app asks in two places and used to answer differently in each.
255	///
256	/// The core is the authority and the answer is not the obvious one:
257	/// `remove_media` refuses while `self.every_clip().any(uses_media)`
258	/// (`core/src/edit_track.rs`), and `every_clip()` is the timeline's clips
259	/// CHAINED with every nest's (`core/src/nest.rs`) — not a walk from the
260	/// timeline down. A nest nothing points at is still in the file and its clips
261	/// still reference media ids, because there is one id space (spec §5.2), so a
262	/// media used only inside an orphaned nest is used.
263	///
264	/// Swift had written the test twice and got it wrong both times: the Media
265	/// tab's Remove and the `remove_media` TOOL each filtered
266	/// `snapshot.clips` — the TOP LEVEL alone. (The tool asks nothing now: the
267	/// core refuses in its own words naming the clips, road map 7's D2·4.) The
268	/// live consequence was that
269	/// removing media used only inside a nest showed no "and its clips" alert at
270	/// all: the pane saw no users, sent a plain `remove_media`, and the core
271	/// refused it, which reaches the user as a bare beep. Phase
272	/// 8c's "unused only" filter would have been a THIRD copy of the same
273	/// mistake, which is what made it worth one file.
274	///
275	/// `ClipSource.mediaID` is the exact mirror of the core's `uses_media`: media,
276	/// still and image clips carry an id and text, shape and nest clips do not.
277	/// A LUT (spec §11 GR-8) is no clip's source but some clips' LOOK: a clip
278	/// uses a media by its source or by its base look, which is the set the
279	/// core's `remove_lut` refuses with and clears (`uses(_:)`). An action end
280	/// naming a LUT is not a use: removing the LUT leaves it inert. A LUT that
281	/// is a media's Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16, `media.color.lut`) is used too:
282	/// `remove_lut` refuses naming those media and clears them
283	/// (`mediaConverted(by:)`).
284	extension ProjectSnapshot {
285	    /// Whether `clip` shows `media` or looks through it.
286	    static func uses(_ clip: ClipSnapshot, _ media: UInt32) -> Bool {
287	        if clip.source.mediaID == media { return true }
288	        guard let look = clip.video?.look else { return false }
289	        return look.kind == .lut && look.media == media
290	    }
291	
292	    /// Every clip that SHOWS this media — the timeline's and every nest's, in
293	    /// that order. What Remove counts and what the "and its clips" alert
294	    /// promises to delete, since `remove_media { with_clips: true }` retains
295	    /// against exactly this set at both levels.
296	    func clipsUsing(_ media: UInt32) -> [ClipSnapshot] {
297	        var used = clips.filter { Self.uses($0, media) }
298	        for nest in nests {
299	            used.append(contentsOf: nest.clips.filter { Self.uses($0, media) })
300	        }
301	        return used
302	    }
303	
304	    /// Whether anything shows it — the question the Media tab's "unused only"
305	    /// filter asks per row, and the one the core asks inside `remove_media`
306	    /// before it refuses.
307	    func usesMedia(_ media: UInt32) -> Bool {
308	        clips.contains { Self.uses($0, media) }
309	            || nests.contains { nest in nest.clips.contains { Self.uses($0, media) } }
310	            || !mediaConverted(by: media).isEmpty
311	    }
312	
313	    /// The media whose Camera Log is the LUT `lut` (spec §11 GR-16), in list
314	    /// order — the core's `media_converted_by`, which `remove_lut` refuses
315	    /// with and clears.
316	    func mediaConverted(by lut: UInt32) -> [MediaSnapshot] {
317	        media.filter { $0.color?.lut == lut }
318	    }
319	
320	    /// The users a SELECTION can hold: the timeline's clips only.
321	    ///
322	    /// Not a narrower version of the same question — a different question,
323	    /// and the reason the two are separate methods rather than one with a
324	    /// flag. `ProjectDocument.clampViewState` intersects the selection with
325	    /// the ids of whatever container is OPEN, so a nested clip has no id the
326	    /// TIMELINE's selection may carry — which is the case Reveal in Timeline
327	    /// has to answer, since it reveals on the timeline. (Road map 2's phase 9
328	    /// made such a clip nameable by an op, through a scope, and openable by a
329	    /// person; what it did not do is let one selection span two containers,
330	    /// and this method is about that.) Reveal in Timeline validates FALSE
331	    /// rather than selecting nothing when this is empty and `clipsUsing` is
332	    /// not — the honest answer being "open the nest first".
333	    func timelineClipsUsing(_ media: UInt32) -> [ClipSnapshot] {
334	        clips.filter { Self.uses($0, media) }
335	    }
336	}

339	/// The seven commands a media row calls back into, and the one question it
340	/// asks: `drop`, `select`, `place`, `revealInTimeline`, `reveal` (in Finder),
341	/// `relink` and `remove`, plus `canRevealInTimeline`.
342	///
343	/// **Why they are a file of their own.** Every one of them applies an edit
344	/// through `binding`, or writes the document's view state, or puts a panel or
345	/// an alert up — which is the pane's business and never a row's
346	/// (`MediaRowView.swift` argues that half) — and none of them touches the
347	/// list's views except `select`, which redraws them. So they are a seam, not
348	/// an amputation: what is left in `MediaPane.swift` is the LIST — its one
349	/// section, its three chrome bands, the find band's arrangement and the Finder
350	/// drop onto the panel.
351	///
352	/// The cut is road map 2's phase 8c paying the ~600-line rule a second time
353	/// for this pane. The first payment (commit b189ac3) moved the row and its
354	/// drag out at 822 lines, precisely so this phase's four additions would have
355	/// room; the additions cost more than the room left, as phase 6 warned they
356	/// would ("budget the cut against the pessimistic number"). It costs ONE
357	/// widening — `MediaPane.rows`, which `select` redraws — which is the toll
358	/// `ExporterLoudness.swift` records for splitting a type across files, and it
359	/// is the whole of it, because everything else here was already internal for
360	/// the row to call.
361	extension MediaPane {
362	    /// Where a dragged row landed. Returns false when the drop is refused, so
363	    /// the drag springs back rather than silently doing nothing.
364	    func drop(_ media: UInt32, on destination: NSView, target: MediaDropTarget) -> Bool {
365	        // A drag started in ANOTHER document's panel must not edit this one:
366	        // the session carries the source row, and the two windows differ.
367	        guard destination.window === window, window != nil else { return false }
368	        guard binding.snapshot.media(media) != nil else { return false }
369	        let fps = binding.canvas.fps
370	        switch target {
371	        case .track(let track, let at, let mode):
372	            let when = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(at, 0), fps: fps)
373	            switch mode {
374	            case .add:
375	                binding.apply("Add Clip", [.addClip(track: track, media: media, at: when)])
376	            case .insert:
377	                binding.apply("Insert", [.insertClip(track: track, media: media, at: when)])
378	            case .overwrite:
379	                binding.apply(
380	                    "Overwrite", [.overwriteClip(track: track, media: media, at: when)])
381	            }
382	        case .canvas:
383	            let at = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(binding.playhead, 0), fps: fps)
384	            let index = binding.snapshot.tracks.count
385	            // `add_track` returns a project, not an id (§11's one entry
386	            // point), so the id is learned from a PURE trial application
387	            // before the real edit runs.
388	            let existing = Set(binding.snapshot.tracks.map { $0.id })
389	            let probed = inspector?.onProbe?([.addTrack(index: index)])
390	            guard let track = probed?.tracks.first(where: { !existing.contains($0.id) })?.id else {
391	                guard let top = binding.snapshot.tracks.last?.id else { return false }
392	                binding.apply("Add Clip", [.addClip(track: top, media: media, at: at)])
393	                return true
394	            }
395	            binding.apply(
396	                "Add Clip",
397	                [.addTrack(index: index), .addClip(track: track, media: media, at: at)])
398	        }
399	        return true
400	    }
401	
402	    /// A row was clicked: it becomes the document's selected media, which is
403	    /// what Edit ▸ Insert / Overwrite at Playhead act on. View state, so it
404	    /// neither dirties the document nor registers an undo step.
405	    func select(_ media: UInt32) {
406	        guard let document = binding.document, document.selectedMedia != media else { return }
407	        document.selectedMedia = media
408	        // The rows draw the selection, and the Edit menu asks for it when it
409	        // validates; the Camera Log section (spec §11 GR-16) reads it too, so
410	        // the pane's controls refresh against the new row.
411	        rows.forEach { $0.view.needsDisplay = true }
412	        refresh()

416	    /// Overwrite at Playhead cannot place a row nobody can see (#68). No work
417	    /// when nothing selected is hidden: `arrange()` calls it on every refresh.
418	    func dropHiddenSelection() {
419	        guard let document = binding.document, let media = document.selectedMedia,
420	              let row = rows.first(where: { $0.media == media }), row.view.isHidden
421	        else { return }
422	        document.selectedMedia = nil
423	        row.view.needsDisplay = true
424	    }

427	    /// Edit menu runs, on the row that was right-clicked.

429	        select(media)

431	              let track = binding.document?.targetTrack
432	        else {
433	            NSSound.beep()
434	            return
435	        }
436	        let at = ReelTime.snapToFrame(max(binding.playhead, 0), fps: binding.canvas.fps)
437	        binding.apply(
438	            insert ? "Insert" : "Overwrite",
439	            [
440	                insert
441	                    ? .insertClip(track: track, media: media, at: at)
442	                    : .overwriteClip(track: track, media: media, at: at)
443	            ])

446	    /// Whether the row menu's Reveal in Timeline has anything to reveal —
447	    /// asked by the row as it builds the menu, so the item is dead rather
448	    /// than silently doing nothing.
449	    ///
450	    /// It is `timelineClipsUsing` and not `clipsUsing` deliberately: media
451	    /// used only INSIDE a nest has users the selection cannot hold
452	    /// (`MediaUsage.swift`), and this is the case the pane's old
453	    /// top-level-only usage test could not tell apart from "used by nothing".
454	    func canRevealInTimeline(_ media: UInt32) -> Bool {
455	        !binding.snapshot.timelineClipsUsing(media).isEmpty
456	    }

458	    /// The row menu's Reveal in Timeline: select every top-level clip that
459	    /// shows this file, and scroll the first one into view.
460	    ///
461	    /// The selection is VIEW state, so this writes it on the document the way
462	    /// `select(_:)` writes `selectedMedia` — no op, no undo step — and then
463	    /// asks the editor to publish it, because the notification and the scroll
464	    /// both belong to the editor (`MediaReveal.swift`).
465	    ///
466	    /// **It throws the panel off this tab, and that is accepted rather than
467	    /// fought.** `InspectorViewController.refresh(isLive:)` switches to the
468	    /// Clip tab whenever a non-empty selection changes, which is the panel's
469	    /// rule for ⌘A, paste and the agent's `set_selection` alike; a command
470	    /// whose whole point is "here are the clips" has no business being the
471	    /// one exception, and the Media tab is one click away.
472	    func revealInTimeline(_ media: UInt32) {
473	        select(media)
474	        let clips = binding.snapshot.timelineClipsUsing(media)
475	        guard !clips.isEmpty, let document = binding.document else {
476	            NSSound.beep()
477	            return
478	        }
479	        document.selection = Set(clips.map { $0.id })
480	        inspector?.onCommand?(#selector(EditorViewController.revealSelectionInTimeline(_:)))
481	    }

484	    func reveal(_ media: UInt32) {

486	            NSSound.beep()
487	            return
488	        }
489	        NSWorkspace.shared.activateFileViewerSelecting([url])
490	    }

492	    /// Relink… — the offer a project whose media has moved opens with (§5.6).
493	    ///
494	    /// **One of three relink paths, and all three probe the new file and
495	    /// owe the cache pass** (spec §11, #63). The chosen file goes to
496	    /// `ProjectDocument.relinkMedia`, the body this path shares with the
497	    /// missing-media sheet: import's own probe, so the entry takes the file's
498	    /// duration, size, rate and flags, a file of another kind is refused in
499	    /// the core's sentence and a clip past a shorter file's end is held to
500	    /// it; one grouped undo step; then `ProjectDocument.generateCaches`, the
501	    /// app's one spelling of "make what is missing", because a relinked file
502	    /// may be one this project has never read — no filmstrip, thumbnail or
503	    /// peaks on disk — and nothing downstream of an edit makes them. The
504	    /// agent's `relink_media` (`AgentServer.relinkMedia`) probes and passes
505	    /// the same way. What the pass costs is its own doc's: a stat, a marker
506	    /// read per half and a `fileExists` per media whose marker still matches,
507	    /// and a rebuild for the one whose file just changed.
508	    func relink(_ media: UInt32) {
509	        guard let entry = binding.snapshot.media(media), let window = window else {
510	            NSSound.beep()
511	            return
512	        }
513	        let binding = self.binding
514	        let panel = NSOpenPanel()
515	        panel.allowsMultipleSelection = false
516	        panel.canChooseDirectories = false
517	        panel.message = "Choose the file for “\(entry.name)”."
518	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { response in
519	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
520	            binding.document?.relinkMedia([(media: media, url: url)])
521	        }
522	    }

524	    /// Remove — refused while the media is in use, with the "and its clips"
525	    /// offer §4.3 asks for.
526	    ///
527	    /// The users are counted through `clipsUsing`, which walks the NESTS as
528	    /// well as the timeline, because that is the set `remove_media` refuses
529	    /// against and the set `with_clips: true` deletes. Filtering
530	    /// `snapshot.clips` here — what this line used to do — meant that media
531	    /// used only inside a compound clip looked unused, went to the core as a
532	    /// plain `remove_media`, came back refused, and reached the user as a
533	    /// beep with the alert never shown (`MediaUsage.swift`).
534	    func remove(_ media: UInt32) {
535	        guard let entry = binding.snapshot.media(media) else {
536	            NSSound.beep()
537	            return
538	        }
539	        // The DOCUMENT's clips, never the scoped view's: `remove_media` is a
540	        // document-level op (`ReelOp.isDocumentLevel`) and is sent unscoped
541	        // even with a nest open, so the "and its clips" count has to be the
542	        // whole file's — the timeline's clips chained with every nest's —
543	        // or the alert would under-count and the op would refuse.
544	        let users = binding.documentSnapshot.clipsUsing(media)
545	        // A LUT that is a media's Camera Log (spec §11 GR-16) is used too:
546	        // `with_clips` clears those conversions with the looks.
547	        let converted = entry.kind == .lut
548	            ? binding.documentSnapshot.mediaConverted(by: media).count : 0
549	        guard !users.isEmpty || converted > 0 else {
550	            binding.apply("Remove Media", [.removeMedia(media: media)])
551	            return
552	        }
553	        guard let window = window else {
554	            NSSound.beep()
555	            return
556	        }
557	        let binding = self.binding
558	        let alert = NSAlert()
559	        alert.messageText = "Remove “\(entry.name)”?"
560	        // A LUT's users keep their place and lose the look (spec §11 GR-8),
561	        // and the files it converts lose their Camera Log (GR-16).
562	        if entry.kind == .lut {
563	            var parts: [String] = []
564	            if !users.isEmpty {
565	                parts.append(
566	                    users.count == 1
567	                        ? "It is the look of 1 clip, which keeps its place and loses the look."
568	                        : "It is the look of \(users.count) clips, which keep their place and "
569	                            + "lose the look.")
570	            }
571	            if converted > 0 {
572	                parts.append(
573	                    (users.isEmpty ? "It is" : "…and")
574	                        + " the Camera Log of \(converted) file\(converted == 1 ? "" : "s"), "
575	                        + "which lose\(converted == 1 ? "s" : "") it.")
576	            }
577	            alert.informativeText = parts.joined(separator: " ")
578	        } else {
579	            alert.informativeText =
580	                users.count == 1
581	                ? "It is used by 1 clip, which will be removed with it."
582	                : "It is used by \(users.count) clips, which will be removed with it."
583	        }
584	        alert.addButton(
585	            withTitle: entry.kind == .lut ? "Remove and Clear Looks" : "Remove and Delete Clips")
586	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
587	        alert.beginSheetModal(for: window) { response in
588	            guard response == .alertFirstButtonReturn else { return }
589	            binding.applyGrouped(
590	                "Remove Media", [.removeMedia(media: media, withClips: true)])
591	        }
592	    }

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an
  older recipe and a file with no `blend` key all render source-over.
- `model_audio.rs` — the audio vocabulary: `AudioProps`, `Compressor`,
  `Limiter` (format 30, spec §11 AU-21, written only when set) and `Duck`
  (with format 29's `DuckMode`, `pre_roll`, `hold` and `DUCK_SPEECH_PAD`)
  and `FadeShape` (`fade_in_shape` / `fade_out_shape`, and
  `Transition.audio_shape`), and their defaults, every format-29 key
  written only when not its default, and `AudioProps.isolation` (format
  31, spec §11 AU-50, 0…1, written only when not 0), and format 32's
  `Equalizer` (seven named slots — `HighPass`, `LowShelf`, `EqBand` × 3,
  `HighShelf`, `LowPass` — and `bypass`), `Hum` and `AudioChannels` (spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-34, each written only when set, `channels` only when not
  `both`), and format 33's `Gate` and `DeEsser` (`audio.gate`,
  `audio.de_esser`, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, after `channels`, each written only
  when set), and format 34's `Voice` (`audio.voice`, spec §11 AU-140, after
  `de_esser`, written only when set: a `VoiceKind` with no default, an
  `amount` defaulting to `VOICE_DEFAULT_AMOUNT`, an optional `pitch`; its
  ranges in `props_check.rs`, its clamp in `actions_clamp.rs`, the chains
  Swift's), and format 37's `Leveller` (`audio.leveller`, spec §11 AU-66:
  `target_db`, `max_up_db`, `max_down_db`, `response`, after `voice`, written
  only when set; its bounds `audio_dynamics.rs`'s); the FIELD `Clip.audio`
  stays in `model.rs`. Re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`; a pure move out of it (road map "audio" AP0), so the audio
  group's new keys land here.
- `audio_eq.rs` — the EQ's and the hum notch's bounds (format 32, spec §11
  AU-31, AU-33, AU-37): `check_eq` / `check_hum`, run by `props_check.rs`'s
  `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence (`audio.eq.<slot>.frequency
  must be between 20 and 20000, not 5`, a slope that is not 12 or 24, mains not
  50 or 60), and `clamp_eq` / `clamp_hum`, run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stage is Swift's.
- `audio_dynamics.rs` — the gate's, the de-esser's and the leveller's bounds
  (format 33, spec §11 AU-43, AU-45, AU-46; format 37, AU-66): `check_gate` /
  `check_de_esser` / `check_leveller`, run by
  `props_check.rs`'s `check_audio` and refusing in the key's own sentence
  (`audio.gate.ratio must be between 1 and 20, not 21`; times through
  `props_check.rs`'s `ticks_in_range`), `check_compressor` /
  `check_limiter` (under a prefix: `audio.` for the clip's, run by
  `check_audio`, and the track's own key for `track_dynamics.rs`, spec §11
  AU-150), and `clamp_gate` / `clamp_de_esser` / `clamp_leveller`
  (each field to its range, NaN to its default), run by `actions_clamp.rs`'s
  `clamp_audio` on an action's end. No sample work; the stages are Swift's.
- `model_text.rs` · `model_shape.rs` · `model_regions.rs` · `model_motion.rs`
  — the text, shape, region and motion vocabularies, each re-exported through
  `model_props.rs`. Text and shape are the two sources the model only
  DESCRIBES and the platform draws and measures: nothing in either file is
  ever a measured size. Regions (`Spotlight`, `ObscureRegion`, `SpotShape`,
  `MAX_OBSCURE`) share one coordinate frame — the centre as an offset in
  SOURCE pixels from the centre of the layer's cropped rect — which
  `edit_zoom.rs` writes out as an equation and nothing else restates. The
  one load-bearing declaration order in these four is `ObscureKind`'s
  (`model_regions.rs`), a shader discriminant like `BlendMode`'s above;
  elsewhere only the JSON spelling of every variant is, so a rename needs a migration step. The enums are closed:
  there is no neutral kind to fall back to.
- `model_words.rs` — the word-caption vocabulary (format version 9, road
  map 8's W1b): `TextCase`, `Word`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill` and
  `WordStyle` (whose `template()` is what `patch.rs`'s text template walks
  against), re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELDS (`case`,
  `words`, `word_style`) close `TextProps`. Format version 12 (spec §11
  W-12) added three looks as KEYS, each off by default: `ActivePill.glide`,
  `WordStyle.active_fill` and `WordStyle.pause_dim` (0–1, range-checked in
  `props_check.rs`); `Word.end` is read by the recipe since then, not only
  by the pager. It also holds the two facts
  every writer of `text.words` shares, both `pub(crate)` and so named
  directly by their callers (a glob re-export cannot widen them):
  `token_count`, THE token rule (`split_whitespace` — the core is the one
  counter, spec §11 W-2), and `rebase_words`, the one saturating
  subtraction `trim_start`, `roll`, `add_transition`'s handle form and
  `split`'s second half make (W-3). Word times are clip-time POSITIONS: a
  negative start is legal, equal starts are legal, and `snap_animation`
  puts them on the grid after `check_text` has named what the caller sent.
- `model_graphic.rs` — the graphic vocabulary (format version 10, road
  map 10): `GraphicProps` (`name`, `width`, `height`, `in`, `length`,
  `props`) and `GRAPHIC_MIN_SIDE` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` and the schema limits
  `GRAPHIC_MAX_PROPS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_OPTIONS` / `GRAPHIC_MAX_STRING` /
  `GRAPHIC_TYPES` (`GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE` restates the engine's `MAX_SIDE` and the
  header's `RC_GRAPHIC_MAX_SIDE`, and each other `GRAPHIC_<X>` the engine's
  `<X>`; `tests/graphic_ffi.rs`'s
  `one_max_side_in_the_engine_the_core_and_the_header` and its four
  `one_…_in_the_engine_and_the_core` tests pin them),
  re-exported through `model_props.rs`; the FIELD `Clip.graphic` stays in
  `model.rs`. And the `pub(crate)` checks every writer shares: `check_name`
  (G-3's `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, its clause `NAME_RULE` shared with
  `validate`), `check_side`, `check_schema` (the engine's sentences, COPIED —

  on an entry is refused, G-41), `check_props` (by dotted
  path against the schema the op carries, shape only without one; a `null`

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

# core/CLAUDE.md — Rust core rules

Applies to everything under `core/`. Build commands and the FFI three-file
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§5 the schemas, §6 the op table, §7 the architecture,
§7.10 this module map in the spec's words; its `README.md` is the index). The long form of
each entry below — why the seam fell where it did — is
`designs/adr/core-file-history.md` (the full history of every cut, with its
line counts, is archived; see its "Original" line); this file is what
governs a module now.

## Module map

- `lib.rs` — module declarations and re-exports only. No implementation code.
- `model.rs` — the spec §5.2 SHAPE: the project, its clips, sources,
  actions, markers and nests (a track is `model_track.rs` and the media
  types `model_media.rs`, both re-exported), with
  the serde defaults that say what an absent key means. The struct field
  names ARE the JSON keys. Nothing else lives here but `CanvasOutput`
  (`Canvas.output`, `sdr` or `hlg`, written only when `hlg`, format 23, spec
  §11 HD-2).
- `model_canvas.rs` — `CanvasBlending` (`Canvas.blending`, `encoded` or
  `linear`, written only when `linear`, format 24, spec §11 GR-18, HD-16),
  re-exported by `model.rs`; the recipe canvas carries it only when linear.
- `model_track.rs` — a track (`Track`, spec §5.2's `tracks[]` and a nest's),
  moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map "audio" AP10's toll T1) and
  re-exported by it; the track vocabulary's new keys land here: format 35's
  `volume` (0…`TRACK_VOLUME_MAX`, 4, written only when not 1) and `pan`
  (−1…1, written only when not 0), spec §11 AU-102, and format 36's
  `compressor` and `limiter` (the clip's `model_audio.rs` types, after `pan`,
  written only when set), spec §11 AU-150.
- `model_media.rs` — the media types (`Media`, `MediaOriginal`, `MediaKind`,
  spec §5.2's `media[]`), moved out of `model.rs` whole (road map
  "creator-jobs" CJ0b's toll T2) and re-exported by it, so every
  `crate::model::Media*` path holds; a media record's new keys land here.
- `model_props.rs` — the schema's VOCABULARY: the per-clip property types
  (`VideoProps`, `Crop`, `Shadow`, `ColorAdjust`, `Chroma`, `Filter`,
  `Reflection`, `BlendMode`) and their defaults (the audio group's are
  `model_audio.rs`'s), re-exported whole by `model.rs` so every
  `crate::model::X` path holds. **`BlendMode`'s, `ObscureKind`'s and
  `TrackMatte`'s declaration ORDER are shader discriminants** (`ProjectSnapshot.swift` and
  `TrackMatte.swift` derive the code from the case index, `Compositor.metal`
  compares against the same integers): append,
  never reorder. `Normal` is 0 with no `+1`, so a zeroed uniform block, an

## Rules

**Modules and size.** New feature area = new module with its own
`impl Project` block. Soft cap ~600 lines; needing a new `// ---- name --`
banner section is the signal to split. Every module keeps a `//!` doc;
numeric and algorithmic choices get prose "why" comments. **A file at the cap
gives something up BEFORE it takes anything on**: the cut is a PURE MOVE,
landed and gated alone, so the feature's diff is attributable; budget the cut
against the pessimistic number, because an estimate here has run about two
thirds of the truth. Over the cap today and known debt, not licence:
`edit.rs`, whose
standing exemption is that its module doc IS the op table's semantics half
(the cut there, if ever forced, is the `Op` enum into an `edit_ops.rs`, and
never in the same phase as a feature). The current list is `wc -l`; named
seams are in `designs/adr/core-file-history.md` "Named next cuts".

**Dependencies.** `serde` and `serde_json` (the JSON the FFI speaks),
`tiny_http` (the agent's socket), and `serde_path_to_error`, which is there
so a patch refusal names the path to what only the type can refuse (a
misspelt variant, a `null` a required field cannot take), where serde alone
names only the value. `graphic` (the path crate `../graphic`, road map
10's motion-graphics engine), named by `ffi_graphic.rs` alone. It enables
`serde_json`'s `preserve_order`, and a feature is unified across a path
dependency, so the core's `serde_json` has it too; `Cargo.toml` spells it
out. `svgtypes` 0.16.1 (usvg's own pin, already in the lock) for its
named-colour table only, so a stored name agrees with what usvg draws
(`model_color.rs`). `sha2` for the `.fjgraphic` manifest's checksums
(G-46; also `graphic_ffi.rs`'s revision oracle).

**One implementation per algorithm.** Before writing time math, find the
existing implementation and route through it. Shared constants have exactly
one home (`TIMESCALE` in `time.rs`; `RC_*` caps in `format.rs`; the
inspector's bounds in `props_check.rs`).

**Purity.** Every edit takes `&self` and returns a new value — internally
clone-then-mutate. An op that would change nothing returns
`Outcome::Identity`, never an identical copy: an identical copy registers a
phantom undo step in the app.

**Errors.** Every edit answers `Result<Outcome, String>` — three arms and
one tier, no error enum. `Outcome::Applied` = the new project;
`Outcome::Identity` = the op is valid and nothing needed to change;
`Outcome::Refused(String)` = a rule declined it, carrying the rule's OWN
sentence rather than a second one written at the call site; `Err(String)` =
invalid arguments, unknown ids, parse failures — lowercase messages naming
the offending value. A refusal is not an error tier: both middle arms leave
the project untouched and register no undo step. No input may panic. FFI
mapping (`ffi_edit.rs`): `Applied` → a new handle; `Identity` → NULL with
neither channel written; `Refused` → NULL with the sentence through
`reason_out`; `Err` → NULL with the message through `err_out`; caught panic
→ `"internal error: <what>"`. The two channels are never both written.

**Times.** Every tick value that reaches the model is snapped to the
document's frame grid before it is stored (`time::snap_to_frame`). Never
store a sub-frame time. Where a range check names the value, the check runs
on what the CALLER sent and the snap follows it, so a refusal never names a
number the door rounded to (`props_check.rs`, `edit_props.rs`'s
`snap_motion` / `snap_animation`). The one family that is deliberately NOT
on the grid is the audio ramps — `audio.fade_in` / `fade_out`, the duck's
and the compressor's attack and release — because they are envelope lengths
sampled at the audio rate, not positions in the picture, and quantising them
to a video frame would round a 10 ms attack to nothing. The other is a SHIFT
(spec §11 #42): an op that moves several clips — the ripples, `close_gap`,
`insert_time`, `move_clip` — moves them all by ONE delta so abutments stay
exact, and at a rate whose frame is not a whole number of ticks (7 fps) a
moved start may sit a tick off the grid; a canvas rate change re-snaps (D7-3).

**FFI exports.** Every export: `#[no_mangle] pub unsafe extern "C"`, a `///`
comment restating the header contract, a `/// # Safety` paragraph, NULL
tolerance first, narrow `unsafe {}` blocks. Route through the shared helpers
in `ffi_util.rs` — a freshly hand-rolled `catch_unwind` is a review flag.
Export names mirror the Rust method exactly.

**Format changes.** Any change to persisted project state bumps
`RC_FORMAT_VERSION` in `format.rs` **and** the `#define` in
`core/include/framejob_core.h`; the reader must keep accepting every prior
version; the writer enforces the reader's caps. A bump whose new fields all
carry a serde default needs no migrate step (versions 3 through 15 have none;
15's one step only renumbers the branch's 1015)
but still bumps, because unknown keys are ignored at every level by design
and an older build would otherwise open the file, drop the new fields on read
and write the loss back on the next save; a bump that changes a field's
SHAPE adds a step at the migration hook (`migrate_1_to_2`). Each bump gets a
`schema_vN.rs` test that opens the previous versions' fixtures and reads the
new keys' ORDER off the written text, since a parsed `Value` sorts them.
**Nothing that checks the version writes the current number as a
literal**, so a bump edits `format.rs` (and `format_history.rs`'s paragraph)
and the header and no test or proof:
- The "one past the current version, refused" tests in
  `core/tests/schema_v3.rs` and `core/tests/model_tests.rs` compute
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION + 1` and assert the refusal's whole message with
  both numbers.
- `schema_v3.rs`'s `the_header_states_the_same_format_version_as_the_core`
  holds the header's `#define` to `format.rs`'s constant, so a bump that
  moves only one of them fails `make test`.
- The schema tests' and `model_tests.rs`'s `/version` assertions read
  `RC_FORMAT_VERSION`; `schema_v10.rs`'s byte-for-byte round trips rewrite
  the fixture's version line through its `current()` helper.
- The proof scripts (`tools/proof/*_proof.py`) read the HEADER's number
  through a `format_version()` helper. `phase9`'s "one past" fixture is
  `format_version() + 1`, and its every-version loop runs up to the current
  version. A proof that expected a literal would fail weeks later, in
  someone else's session, with nothing pointing at the bump.

A fixture's own version (`e2_proof.py`'s `VERSION = 8`, a
`schema_vN.rs`'s older files) is a literal on purpose. One claim still
moves with the schema rather than the number: when a bump appends a key to
the video object, `schema_v4.rs`'s text assertion about what follows
`obscure` fails in `make test` and names the new neighbour.

**Tests.** All tests are black-box in `core/tests/` (no `#[cfg(test)]` in
`src/`), exercised **through the FFI** wherever possible, and verified
against independently written oracles — never golden files. Shared helpers
live in `tests/common/` (`content` / `contents` — "the same clips, ids
aside" — is the one spelling of that comparison, used by `nest`'s identity
claim and `scope`'s oracle alike); new feature area = new test file. Every
new export gets at least one test plus inclusion in the null-safety sweep.
Finish Rust work with `cargo fmt` and a clean `make lint`.

</system-reminder>

229	            return
